chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from 'Abd Allah ibn Muskan, from Ishaq ibn 'Ammar, from Abi Basir, who said:

I asked Aba 'Abd Allah عليه السلام about a mutamatti' who intended to shorten his hair, but shaved his head. He said: A blood-offering is upon him, which he must spill; then when the Day of Sacrifice comes, he should pass the razor over his head when he intends to shave.
Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: Blood is only required of him if he did that deliberately. But if he did it forgetfully, then nothing is upon him; that which indicates this is as follows.

key_terms.الْمُوسَى: the razor passed over the head for shaving
key_terms.دَمٌ: a sacrificial blood-offering due as compensation
key_terms.فَحَلَقَ: then he shaved, instead of shortening
key_terms.يَوْمُ النَّحْرِ: the Day of Sacrifice during hajj rites
key_terms.يُقَصِّرَ: to shorten the hair as required in the rite

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a pilgrim in tamattu' shaves his head instead of shortening it?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses the ruling for a pilgrim performing tamattu' who shaves his head instead of merely shortening his hair before the proper time. It states that a blood-offering is due if this was done deliberately, while no liability applies if it was done forgetfully, and he should still pass the razor over his head on the Day of Sacrifice.
